instructions: Put a large pot of water on to boil over high heat.

Meanwhile, make the sauce. In a small bowl, stir the 4 tsp cornstarch into the 2 tbsp dark soy sauce until there are no lumps. Stir in 2 tbsp light soy sauce, 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine, 1 tsp sugar, 1/2 tsp sesame oil, 1/4 tsp white pepper and 1/4 cup water.

Stem and slice the 4 oz mushrooms. Thinly slice half the onion. Seed the bell pepper and slice it into strips. Peel the 2 carrots and cut them into thin sticks about 2 inches long. Mince the 2 garlic cloves.
Trim the 4 oz snow peas. Slice the 2 heads of bok choy across into 1 inch pieces. Cut 6 of the scallions into 2 inch lengths.

Cook the 1 lb noodles in the boiling water until they're just tender, about 2 to 3 minutes for fresh noodles, or the time on the package. Drain them, rinse under cold water and shake off as much water as you can.

Heat a wok or your largest skillet over high heat until it starts to smoke. Add 1 tbsp of the oil and the mushrooms in one layer. Leave them for 2 minutes, until they're browned underneath, then stir and cook for 1 minute. Tip them onto a plate.
Add the last 1 tbsp oil, then the onion and garlic. Stir for 30 seconds, until they smell fragrant.
Add the carrots and pepper and stir fry for 2 minutes, until they're just starting to soften.
Add the snow peas and bok choy and stir fry for 1 minute, until the leaves have wilted and the stems are still crisp.
Add the noodles and the mushrooms. Stir the sauce again and pour it over. Toss with two spoons or tongs for 30 seconds, lifting the noodles up from the bottom.
Add the scallions and toss for 1 minute, until the sauce has thickened and every noodle is coated and brown.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve it right away, straight from the pan.
method_notes: All three boil the noodles first and toss them last in a soy sauce based sauce, after a fast stir fry of vegetables in a very hot wok. RecipeTin Eats thickens its sauce of dark and light soy, cooking wine, sugar, sesame oil and white pepper with cornstarch and water, starts with onion and garlic, and makes it with chicken or another protein alongside carrot, pepper and green onion. The Woks of Life leaves out the cornstarch, starts with mushrooms and adds snow peas and leafy greens; Omnivore's Cookbook uses snow peas, carrot, baby bok choy and ginger. This one follows RecipeTin Eats' sauce and order, browns shiitake in place of the meat and adds the snow peas and bok choy from the other two.
